text:
kai: Heads-up — HF->Redwood conversion for openlm-3b failed our tokenizer sanity check. tokenizer.json and tokenizer_config.json disagree on special tokens and there is no fast vocab file. Error snippet below.

kai: ```
ValueError: Tokenizer mismatch: tokenizer_config.json reports vocab_size=null, tokenizer.json has 50272 tokens. Fast loader aborted, falling back to SlowTokenizer which doesn't map <s>/<cls> -> generation broken.
```

marta: Can you paste the two files (first 20 lines) or a diff? fast vs slow mismatch usually obvious.

kai: Pasted diffs:
```
--- tokenizer.json
+  "special_tokens": {"cls_token": "<s>", "sep_token": "</s>", "pad_token": "<pad>"},
+  "model_max_length": 2048,
--- tokenizer_config.json
-  "cls_token": null,
-  "model_max_length": 1024,
-  "vocab_size": null
```

kai: tokenizer.json is a single-file Tokenizers artifact (fast) but it doesn't ship separate vocab.txt/merges or vocab.json that our HF->Redwood loader expects. tokenizer_config.json appears to be an auto-generated stub missing specials.

chris: This is the classic fast vs slow loader gap. Our loader currently prefers tokenizer_config.json fields for special tokens, then falls back to tokenizers lib only if tokenizer_config contains expected keys. If tokenizer.json exists but missing external vocab files we end up with inconsistent runtime mapping.

swapnil: Quick workaround that worked for me locally: load Tokenizer from tokenizer.json and export a minimal tokenizer_config.json with the special tokens and vocab_size. Eg: `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json'); print({'vocab_size': t.get_vocab_size()})"` then write out the expected keys. Also creating a vocab.json from `t.get_vocab()` and adding to the repo fixed the fast loader path.

ash: (typo: ash) Is this what caused the quantization eval regressions? Our 4-bit runs for the candidate model had shorter outputs and lower Rouge on convo tests.

kai: Yes, evals show ~8% drop in ROUGE and truncation on prompts where system role had tokens that the slow loader normalized differently. Chat templates were tokenized inconsistently so routing/stop tokens didn't match.

build-bot: CI: model-onboard/185 failed — tokenizer loader error: Missing "vocab_size" in tokenizer_config.json (see logs: ci/build-185.log).

chris: I'll update the HF->Redwood converter to: 1) if tokenizer.json present, prefer using tokenizers.Tokenizer.from_file and synthesize tokenizer_config.json with specials and vocab_size; 2) add clearer error with recommended quickfix; 3) add unit test to catch model_max_length mismatch. Will push RFC & small patch.

kai: Thanks. I'll open a PR with the quickfix script and test artifacts (symlinked vocab.json + small regen script) so CI can re-run. Posting PR in a bit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/NNN.

marta: Nice. Also let's add a short doc blurb under model-onboarding describing the tokenizer.json vs tokenizer_config contract and common HF export pitfalls. Saves future confusion. :+1:

chris: Agreed — will add to the onboarding checklist and the converter's README.

kai: For tracking: recording this in the model-onboard ticket and adding the failing model id (openlm-3b-2204) so we can re-run after patch.
